codes.meaning: The touch-control module is having trouble communicating internally.
The cooking surface is still too hot to register as safe, and clears on its own once it cools.
Something pressing on the control panel is being misread as a touch input.
The electronics underneath have gotten too hot, so the cooktop shuts the panel off until it cools.
The cookware on a zone isn't magnetic-compatible, isn't centered properly, or is the wrong size.
That zone is still hot to the touch, either from recent use or heat carried over from a neighboring zone.
Power to the unit was interrupted long enough that the freezer compartment warmed to 18°F or higher.
The freezer side has stayed above 15°F for more than roughly 90 minutes.
Points to trouble in the oven's temperature-sensing circuit — the sensor, control board, or wiring.
Indicates the keypad/user-interface panel, control board, or connecting wiring is malfunctioning.
General oven-control fault, covering the control board itself or its wiring harness.
The oven (or warming-drawer) temperature sensor or its wiring is suspected of failing.
A wall-oven variant of the control/wiring fault family.
Signals an electronics fault in the commercial range's control system.

F2E1.what_it_means: An electronics fault in the range's control system.
F2E1.why_it_happens: A control-board or keypad failure, not a cooking setting or a door condition.
F2E1.what_to_try: Cutting power at the breaker for a minute clears a one-off glitch. A code that returns is naming a real fault.
F2E1.when_to_call: If it returns after a power cycle, the control needs replacing or repairing.

codes.meaning: The main control module itself is the suspected point of failure.
The wash motor isn't behaving as expected and needs a power cycle to attempt recovery.
The water inlet (fill) valve is stuck open, letting water in when it shouldn't.
Water isn't draining out fast enough, usually from a blockage somewhere in the drain path.

F9E1.what_it_means: Water is not draining out fast enough, usually from a blockage in the drain path.
F9E1.why_it_happens: A clogged tub filter, a kinked hose, or a silted-up air gap on the worktop.
F9E1.what_to_try: Clear the tub filter, check the air gap, then the drain hose.
F9E1.when_to_call: If the filter and hose are clear and it still will not drain, the drain pump needs testing.

codes.meaning: The dishwasher isn't sensing water coming in at all.
Water has been detected pooling in the drip tray underneath the unit.

F8E4.what_it_means: Water has been detected pooling in the drip tray underneath the unit.
F8E4.why_it_happens: A leak above the tray rather than a drainage problem inside the tub.
F8E4.what_to_try: Turn the supply off at the valve and stop using the machine until the leak is traced.
F8E4.when_to_call: This needs a technician — the tray only tells you water arrived, not where from.

washer.note: KitchenAid publishes an error-code list for DISHWASHERS only. For washers there are owner's manuals with symptom troubleshooting (won't fill, won't drain, won't spin) but no displayed-code list. Service tech sheets exist as PDFs but are service literature, not owner-facing published codes.

codes.meaning: A power interruption was long enough for internal temperatures to climb past the safe threshold.
The fresh-food compartment has held above 48°F for an extended stretch, indicating a real cooling problem.
The unit's interior has gotten colder than it should.
